source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substring including written/read and other annotations.
source.public_versification_note: Exact XML records mapped to public labels; Zechariah 1:18–2:13 and Malachi 4 have different Hebrew chapter boundaries.

delta_method: F0 retained; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential choices flagged by the selective apparatus. Classification remains provisional. Overlap is triage only, with no change quota.

comparative_references.scope: Programmatic alignment after recovery of unfinished original-language drafts; selected bilingual rereads recorded separately. TSW is not the base text.

verses.rationale: Retains date and both ancestral names without deciding the title’s grammatical attachment beyond the familiar apposition.
verses.before: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:
verses.after: In the eighth month of Darius’s second year, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:

verses.rationale: Preserves the emphatic anger opening.
verses.before: “The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.
verses.after: “The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.

verses.rationale: Retains all three divine-name formulas and the return/return reciprocity.
verses.before: So say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Return to me, says the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Tell them: The LORD of Armies says, ‘Return to me,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will return to you,’ says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore say to them: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Return to me, says the LORD of Hosts, and I will return to you, says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps ways/deeds paired and makes the nested prophetic speech clear.
verses.before: Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Return now from your evil ways and from your evil deeds.’ But they did not hear or pay attention to me, says the LORD.
verses.after: ‘Do not be like your ancestors. The earlier prophets called to them: The LORD of Armies says, “Turn back from your evil ways and evil deeds.” But they would not listen or pay attention to me,’ declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying, ‘Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Return now from your evil ways and from your evil deeds.’ But they did not hear or pay attention to me, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains both questions without supplying answers.
verses.before: Your ancestors—where are they? And the prophets—do they live forever?
verses.after: ‘Your ancestors—where are they? And the prophets—do they live forever?
verses.tsw_comparator: Your ancestors—where are they? And the prophets—do they live forever?

verses.rationale: Keeps the overtaking image and repeated ways/deeds in the response.
verses.before: But my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your ancestors?” Then they returned and said, “Just as the LORD of Hosts intended to do to us according to our ways and our deeds, so the LORD has dealt with us.”
verses.after: But did not my words and decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, overtake your ancestors?’ Then they turned back and said, ‘The LORD of Armies has done to us just as he planned, in keeping with our ways and deeds.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: But my words and my statutes, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your ancestors?” Then they returned and said, “Just as the LORD of Hosts intended to do to us according to our ways and our deeds, so the LORD has dealt with us.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all date details and repeats the full prophetic identification.
verses.before: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:
verses.after: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in Darius’s second year, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:
verses.tsw_comparator: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:

verses.rationale: Retains the rider, hollow, myrtles, and three colors without identifying symbolic nations.
verses.before: I saw in the night, and there was a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.
verses.after: During the night I saw a man riding a red horse. He stood among the myrtle trees in the hollow, with red, sorrel, and white horses behind him.
verses.tsw_comparator: I saw in the night, and there was a man riding on a red horse. He was standing among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were red, sorrel, and white horses.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes the interpreting angel from the seen rider while preserving the question.
verses.before: Then I said, “My lord, what are these?” And the angel who was speaking with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”
verses.after: I asked, “What are these, my lord?” The angel speaking with me answered, “I will show you what they are.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “My lord, what are these?” And the angel who was speaking with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the rider’s reply and earthly patrol.
verses.before: Then the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered, “These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”
verses.after: The man standing among the myrtles said, “These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered, “These are the ones whom the LORD has sent to patrol the earth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the report’s troubling peace without equating it with justice.
verses.before: And they answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees and said, “We have patrolled the earth, and look—the entire earth is still and at rest.”
verses.after: They answered the angel of the LORD standing among the myrtles: “We have patrolled the earth, and look—the whole earth is settled and quiet.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees and said, “We have patrolled the earth, and look—the whole earth is still and at rest.”

verses.rationale: Retains intercession, both regions, and the exact seventy years.
verses.before: Then the angel of the LORD answered and said, “O LORD of Hosts, how long will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, against which you have been angry these seventy years?”
verses.after: Then the angel of the LORD said, “LORD of Armies, how long will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel of the LORD answered and said, “O LORD of Hosts, how long will you withhold compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, against which you have been angry these seventy years?”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated words and comforting answer.
verses.before: And the LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with good words, comforting words.
verses.after: The LORD answered the angel speaking with me with good words, words of comfort.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with good words, comforting words.

verses.rationale: Keeps jealousy and both city designations rather than replacing with generic concern.
verses.before: Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me, “Proclaim, saying: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I am deeply jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion,
verses.after: The angel speaking with me said, “Proclaim this: The LORD of Armies says, ‘I am deeply jealous for Jerusalem and Zion.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me, “Proclaim, saying: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: I am deeply jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion,

verses.rationale: Preserves the contrast between divine anger and the nations’ aggravation of harm.
verses.before: and I am very angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was angry only a little, but they made the disaster worse.
verses.after: I am very angry with the nations at ease. I was angry for a little while, but they made the harm worse.’
verses.tsw_comparator: and I am very angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was angry only a little, but they made the disaster worse.

verses.rationale: Keeps restoration, rebuilding, and measuring as distinct actions.
verses.before: So, thus says the LORD: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be built in it, says the LORD of Hosts, and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.
verses.after: So the LORD says, ‘I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt within her,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and a measuring line will be stretched over Jerusalem.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore, thus says the LORD: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house shall be built in it, says the LORD of Hosts, and a measuring line shall be stretched over Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated again and both comfort and choice.
verses.before: Proclaim again, saying: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: My cities will again overflow with good, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”
verses.after: Proclaim again: The LORD of Armies says, ‘My cities will again overflow with good things. The LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Proclaim again, saying: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: My cities shall again overflow with good, and the LORD shall again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the count and unexplained initial vision image.
verses.before: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four horns.
verses.after: I looked up and saw four horns.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four horns.

verses.rationale: Preserves all three named communities in the interpretation.
verses.before: I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these?” And he said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
verses.after: I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these?” He answered, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these?” And he said to me, “These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the matching count without narrowing the craft prematurely.
verses.before: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
verses.after: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

verses.rationale: Retains head and horn imagery and explains the action’s referents through demonstratives.
verses.before: I said, “What are these coming to do?” He said, “These are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could raise their head. But these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
verses.after: I asked, “What have they come to do?” He answered, “Those horns scattered Judah so thoroughly that no one could lift his head. These have come to terrify them and throw down the horns of the nations that raised a horn against Judah’s land to scatter it.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said, “What are these coming to do?” He said, “These are the horns that scattered Judah so completely that no one could raise their head. But these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated viewing formula and concrete measuring implement.
verses.before: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man with a measuring line in his hand.
verses.after: I looked up and saw a man with a measuring cord in his hand.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man with a measuring line in his hand.

verses.rationale: Keeps both dimensions and the intended action.
verses.before: I said, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what its width is and what its length is.”
verses.after: I asked, “Where are you going?” He answered, “To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide and how long it is.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said, “Where are you going?” He said to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what its width is and what its length is.”

verses.rationale: Maintains two angels without merging their roles.
verses.before: Then the angel who was speaking with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him.
verses.after: Then the angel speaking with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel who was speaking with me went out, and another angel came out to meet him.

verses.rationale: Retains the unwalled-settlement image and includes animals in abundance.
verses.before: And he said to him, “Run, speak to that young man, saying: Jerusalem will be inhabited like villages without walls because of the multitude of people and livestock within it.
verses.after: He said to him, “Run and tell that young man: ‘Jerusalem will be inhabited like open country because of the many people and animals within her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to him, “Run, speak to that young man, saying: Jerusalem shall be inhabited like villages without walls because of the multitude of people and livestock within it.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two forms of divine presence, surrounding and within.
verses.before: I myself will be for it, says the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be glory in its midst.”
verses.after: I myself will be a wall of fire around her,’ declares the LORD, ‘and I will be glory within her.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I myself will be for it, says the LORD, a wall of fire all around, and I will be glory in its midst.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated summons and four-winds comparison.
verses.before: “Ho! Ho! Flee from the land of the north, says the LORD, for I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven, says the LORD.
verses.after: “Come! Come! Flee from the land of the north,” declares the LORD. “For I have spread you out like the four winds of heaven,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Ho! Ho! Flee from the land of the north, says the LORD, for I have scattered you like the four winds of heaven, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two city personifications and exile setting.
verses.before: Ho, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with daughter Babylon.
verses.after: “Come, Zion! Escape, you who live with daughter Babylon!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Ho, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with daughter Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keeps the difficult after-glory clause, sent speaker, and his-eye pronoun without silent harmonization.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: After glory, he sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
verses.after: For the LORD of Armies says—after glory he sent me to the nations that plundered you—“Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: After glory, he sent me against the nations that plundered you, for whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.

verses.rationale: Retains the reversal between enslavers and slaves and the recognition formula.
verses.before: For look, I am about to wave my hand over them, and they will become plunder for people who served them. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me.
verses.after: I will wave my hand over them, and they will become plunder for their own slaves.” Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am about to wave my hand over them, and they shall become plunder for those who served them. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me.

verses.rationale: Keeps direct promise, dwelling, and feminine personification.
verses.before: Sing and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, says the LORD.
verses.after: “Sing and rejoice, daughter Zion! I am coming, and I will dwell among you,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Sing and rejoice, daughter Zion, for look, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the consequential shifts among LORD, my, I, and me rather than deciding the speaker’s identity in translation.
verses.before: Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they will become my people. I will dwell in your midst, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.
verses.after: “Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people. I will dwell among you.” Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Many nations shall join themselves to the LORD on that day, and they shall become my people. And I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.

verses.rationale: Retains inheritance language, holy land, and renewed choice.
verses.before: The LORD will inherit Judah as a portion in the holy land and will again choose Jerusalem.
verses.after: The LORD will take Judah as his own portion in the holy land and will again choose Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD will inherit Judah as a portion in the holy land and will again choose Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Keeps the all-flesh address and awakening image.
verses.before: Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for the LORD has roused himself from his holy dwelling.
verses.after: Be silent before the LORD, all flesh! He has stirred from his holy dwelling.
verses.tsw_comparator: Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD, for the LORD has roused himself from his holy dwelling.

verses.rationale: Retains the accuser’s role and its repeated verb without prematurely imposing a proper name.
verses.before: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and the accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
verses.after: He showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, with the accuser at his right hand to accuse him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and the accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three LORD occurrences and the rescued-brand question.
verses.before: And the LORD said to the accuser, “The LORD rebuke you, O accuser! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a burning brand plucked from the fire?”
verses.after: The LORD said to the accuser, “The LORD rebuke you, accuser! The LORD who chooses Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a burning stick snatched from the fire?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to the accuser, “The LORD rebuke you, O accuser! The LORD who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Is this not a burning brand plucked from the fire?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the concrete clothing and position.
verses.before: Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.
verses.after: Joshua stood before the angel wearing filthy clothes.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments as he stood before the angel.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes command to attendants from assurance to Joshua and connects guilt with clothing removal.
verses.before: And the angel answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I will clothe you in festal garments.”
verses.after: The angel told those standing before him, “Take off his filthy clothes.” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have removed your guilt from you, and I will dress you in fine robes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the angel answered and said to those standing before him, “Remove the filthy garments from him.” Then he said to Joshua, “See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I will clothe you in festal garments.”

verses.rationale: Follows the pinned I-said reading and preserves the prophet’s participation.
verses.before: I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they put the clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
verses.after: I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they placed a clean turban on his head and dressed him, while the angel of the LORD stood nearby.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said, “Let them put a clean turban on his head.” So they put the clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.

verses.rationale: Retains the solemn transition to conditional instruction.
verses.before: Then the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:
verses.after: The angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:

verses.rationale: Preserves both conditions and both responsibilities, with access among attendants left unexplained.
verses.before: “Thus says the LORD of Hosts: If you walk in my ways and if you keep my charge, then you will govern my house and keep my courts, and I will give you access among these who are standing here.
verses.after: “The LORD of Armies says, ‘If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, you will govern my house and guard my courts. I will give you access among these who stand here.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus says the LORD of Hosts: If you walk in my ways and if you keep my charge, then you shall govern my house and keep my courts, and I will give you access among these who are standing here.

verses.rationale: Keeps sign-men and the Branch title without identifying its fulfillment.
verses.before: Hear now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are people who are a sign: Look, I am bringing my servant, the Branch.
verses.after: Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions seated before you—for they are men who serve as signs. I am bringing my servant, the Branch.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hear now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are people who are a sign: Look, I am bringing my servant, the Branch.

verses.rationale: Retains one stone, seven eyes, inscription, and single day as distinct details.
verses.before: For look at the stone that I have set before Joshua. On this one stone are seven eyes. Look, I will engrave its inscription, says the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.
verses.after: Look at the stone I have set before Joshua: on that one stone are seven eyes. I will engrave its inscription,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘and I will remove the guilt of that land in a single day.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look at the stone that I have set before Joshua. On this one stone are seven eyes. Look, I will engrave its inscription, says the LORD of Hosts, and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.

verses.rationale: Keeps the concrete peace-and-hospitality image.
verses.before: On that day, says the LORD of Hosts, each of you will invite your neighbor to sit under the vine and under the fig tree.”
verses.after: On that day,’ declares the LORD of Armies, ‘each of you will invite his neighbor under his vine and fig tree.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, says the LORD of Hosts, each of you shall invite your neighbor to sit under the vine and under the fig tree.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the simile rather than declaring the vision a dream.
verses.before: Then the angel who was speaking with me returned and woke me, like someone awakened from sleep.
verses.after: The angel speaking with me returned and roused me, as someone is awakened from sleep.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel who was speaking with me returned and woke me, like someone awakened from sleep.

verses.rationale: Follows the read I-answered form and renders the repeated seven distributively, with the construction noted.
verses.before: And he said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see, and look—a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on its top and seven lamps on it, with seven channels for each of the lamps that are on its top.
verses.after: He asked, “What do you see?” I answered, “A lampstand entirely of gold, with a bowl on top and seven lamps on it, and seven channels for each of the lamps on top.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see, and look—a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on its top and seven lamps on it, with seven channels for each of the lamps that are on its top.

verses.rationale: Retains exact bilateral arrangement.
verses.before: And there are two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left.”
verses.after: Beside it are two olive trees, one to the bowl’s right and one to its left.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And there are two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the question open rather than substituting an interpretation.
verses.before: Then I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
verses.after: I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”

verses.rationale: Makes the exchange easy to follow while preserving both responses.
verses.before: The angel who was speaking with me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
verses.after: He answered, “Do you not know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I said.
verses.tsw_comparator: The angel who was speaking with me answered and said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” And I said, “No, my lord.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes force from power and retains the central spirit contrast.
verses.before: Then he answered and said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, and not by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: He said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: ‘Not by military strength, nor by power, but by my spirit,’ says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he answered and said to me, “This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might, and not by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps mountain, top stone, and the repeated grace acclamation.
verses.before: Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. And he will bring out the top stone with shouts of, ‘Grace, grace to it!’”
verses.after: Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become level ground. He will bring out the top stone amid shouts of ‘Grace, grace to it!’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Who are you, O great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you shall become a plain. And he shall bring out the top stone with shouts of, ‘Grace, grace to it!’”

verses.rationale: Retains the new prophetic-word introduction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Retains repeated hands, beginning/completion, and sent-speaker formula.
verses.before: “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.
verses.after: “Zerubbabel’s hands laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands shall finish it. Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you.

verses.rationale: Connects seven to the eyes while retaining the uncertain tin/plumb stone image in a note.
verses.before: For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which range through the entire earth.”
verses.after: Who has despised the day of small things? These seven will rejoice when they see the plumb stone in Zerubbabel’s hand. They are the eyes of the LORD, ranging through the whole earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which range through the whole earth.”

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated question and positions.
verses.before: Then I answered and said to him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and on the left of the lampstand?”
verses.after: I asked him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and left of the lampstand?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I answered and said to him, “What are these two olive trees on the right and on the left of the lampstand?”

verses.rationale: Preserves literal gold rather than silently substituting oil in the vision.
verses.before: And a second time I answered and said to him, “What are the two branches of the olive trees beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil?”
verses.after: I asked him a second time, “What are the two olive branches beside the two golden pipes that pour out the gold?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a second time I answered and said to him, “What are the two branches of the olive trees beside the two golden pipes that pour out the golden oil?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the repeated ignorance-and-answer exchange.
verses.before: And he said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”
verses.after: He said, “Do you not know what these are?” “No, my lord,” I answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “Do you not know what these are?” I said, “No, my lord.”

verses.rationale: Renders the sons-of-oil idiom as anointed ones; retains the literal expression in the note without assigning the figures identities.
verses.before: Then he said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
verses.after: He said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said, “These are the two anointed ones who stand beside the Lord of all the earth.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the recurring look and the surprising object.
verses.before: Again I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a flying scroll.
verses.after: Again I looked up and saw a flying scroll.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a flying scroll.

verses.rationale: Retains exact numbers and ancient units.
verses.before: And he said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying scroll. Its length is twenty cubits, and its width ten cubits.”
verses.after: He asked me, “What do you see?” I answered, “A flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “What do you see?” I said, “I see a flying scroll. Its length is twenty cubits, and its width ten cubits.”

verses.rationale: Chooses swept-away and two-sided reading for difficult wording, with alternatives identified in notes.
verses.before: Then he said to me, “This is the curse going out over the face of the whole land. For everyone who steals will be removed according to what is written on one side, and everyone who swears falsely will be removed according to what is written on the other side.
verses.after: He said, “This is the curse going out over the whole land. Every thief will be swept away according to what is on one side, and everyone who swears will be swept away according to what is on the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he said to me, “This is the curse going out over the face of the whole land. For everyone who steals shall be removed according to what is written on one side, and everyone who swears falsely shall be removed according to what is written on the other side.

verses.rationale: Retains the curse’s entering, remaining, and consuming actions and both materials.
verses.before: I have sent it out, says the LORD of Hosts, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will remain in that house and consume it, both its timber and its stones.”
verses.after: I have sent it out,” declares the LORD of Armies. “It will enter the thief’s house and the house of anyone who swears falsely by my name. It will stay inside that house and consume it, timbers and stones alike.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I have sent it out, says the LORD of Hosts, and it shall enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It shall remain in that house and consume it, both its timber and its stones.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the new vision summons distinct.
verses.before: Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me, “Lift your eyes and see what this is that is going out.”
verses.after: The angel speaking with me came forward and said, “Look up and see what is coming out.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me, “Lift your eyes and see what this is that is going out.”

verses.rationale: Preserves ephah and the pinned eye/appearance reading rather than silently changing to iniquity.
verses.before: I said, “What is it?” He said, “This is the ephah that is going out.” And he said, “This is their appearance throughout the whole land.”
verses.after: I asked, “What is it?” He answered, “An ephah basket coming out.” He added, “This is their appearance throughout the land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I said, “What is it?” He said, “This is the ephah that is going out.” And he said, “This is their appearance throughout the whole land.”

verses.rationale: Retains the woman, material, and container without allegorical expansion.
verses.before: And look—a round cover of lead was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah.
verses.after: A lead cover was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah basket.
verses.tsw_comparator: And look—a round cover of lead was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the ephah.

verses.rationale: Retains the explicit personification and forceful confinement.
verses.before: And he said, “This is Wickedness.” Then he threw her back into the ephah and threw the lead weight over its opening.
verses.after: He said, “This is Wickedness.” He pushed her back into the ephah basket and threw the lead weight over its opening.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said, “This is Wickedness.” Then he threw her back into the ephah and threw the lead weight over its opening.

verses.rationale: Keeps female winged figures, the stork comparison, and the airborne position.
verses.before: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were two women coming forward, with wind in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted the ephah between earth and heaven.
verses.after: I looked up and saw two women coming forward, with wind in their wings. Their wings were like a stork’s. They lifted the ephah basket between earth and heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were two women coming forward, with wind in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted the ephah between earth and heaven.

verses.rationale: Preserves the destination question rather than anticipating its answer.
verses.before: Then I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “Where are they taking the ephah?”
verses.after: I asked the angel speaking with me, “Where are they taking the ephah basket?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said to the angel who was speaking with me, “Where are they taking the ephah?”

verses.rationale: Retains Shinar and installation on a base without asserting an unstated cultic identification.
verses.before: And he said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When it is prepared, it will be set there on its base.”
verses.after: He answered, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When it is ready, the basket will be set there on its base.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to me, “To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When it is prepared, it will be set there on its base.”

verses.rationale: Retains all counts and the mountains’ extraordinary material.
verses.before: Again I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
verses.after: Again I looked up and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains. The mountains were made of bronze.
verses.tsw_comparator: Again I lifted my eyes and looked, and there were four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact order and colors.
verses.before: The first chariot had red horses, the second chariot black horses,
verses.after: The first chariot had red horses, and the second had black horses.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first chariot had red horses, the second chariot black horses,

verses.rationale: Preserves strength alongside the fourth team’s color pattern.
verses.before: the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot strong dappled horses.
verses.after: The third had white horses, and the fourth had strong, dappled horses.
verses.tsw_comparator: the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot strong dappled horses.

verses.rationale: Retains the recurring request for interpretation.
verses.before: Then I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
verses.after: I asked the angel speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I answered and said to the angel who was speaking with me, “What are these, my lord?”

verses.rationale: Chooses winds with spirits as an alternative in the note, and retains their prior attendance.
verses.before: The angel answered and said to me, “These are the four winds of heaven going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.
verses.after: The angel answered, “These are the four winds of heaven, going out after standing before the Lord of all the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: The angel answered and said to me, “These are the four winds of heaven going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of all the earth.

verses.rationale: Follows behind-them rather than a conjectured western destination.
verses.before: The chariot with the black horses is going toward the land of the north, the white ones are going out after them, and the dappled ones are going toward the land of the south.
verses.after: The black horses are going to the northern land; the white horses follow them. The dappled horses are going to the southern land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The chariot with the black horses is going toward the land of the north, the white ones are going out after them, and the dappled ones are going toward the land of the south.

verses.rationale: Retains the threefold patrol language and leaves the unnamed commander unnamed.
verses.before: When the strong horses came out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth. And he said, “Go, patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.
verses.after: The strong horses came out, eager to patrol the earth. He said, “Go, patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the strong horses came out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth. And he said, “Go, patrol the earth.” So they patrolled the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves spirit/rest and the repeated destination without collapsing the image to anger alone.
verses.before: Then he called out to me and spoke to me, saying, “Look, those going toward the land of the north have given my Spirit rest in the land of the north.”
verses.after: Then he called out to me, “Look, those going to the northern land have brought my spirit to rest in the northern land.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then he called out to me and spoke to me, saying, “Look, those going toward the land of the north have given my Spirit rest in the land of the north.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the new oracle introduction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to me:

verses.rationale: Clarifies the donors and destination while retaining all four names and Babylon.
verses.before: “Take from the exiles Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon. On that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
verses.after: “Take gifts from the exiles—from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon. Go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Take from the exiles Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon. On that same day go to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

verses.rationale: Retains the plural crowns and the named priest rather than substituting Zerubbabel.
verses.before: Take silver and gold, make crowns, and set a crown upon the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
verses.after: Take silver and gold, make crowns, and place them on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
verses.tsw_comparator: Take silver and gold, make crowns, and set a crown upon the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Branch/branch wordplay and building task.
verses.before: And say to him: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, a man whose name is Branch. From his place he will branch out, and he will build the temple of the LORD.
verses.after: Tell him: The LORD of Armies says, ‘Here is a man whose name is Branch. He will branch out from his place and build the LORD’s temple.
verses.tsw_comparator: And say to him: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, a man whose name is Branch. From his place he shall branch out, and he shall build the temple of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves the two figures permitted by the final clause and notes the priest-on-throne alternative.
verses.before: He will build the temple of the LORD; he will bear majesty and will sit and rule on his throne. There will also be a priest by his throne, and peaceful counsel will be between the two.
verses.after: He will build the LORD’s temple. He will bear majesty and sit and rule on his throne. A priest will be at his throne, and peaceful counsel will be between the two of them.’
verses.tsw_comparator: He shall build the temple of the LORD; he shall bear majesty and shall sit and rule on his throne. There shall also be a priest by his throne, and peaceful counsel shall be between the two.

verses.rationale: Retains the names as written here instead of harmonizing Helem/Hen with verse ten.
verses.before: And the crowns will be in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.
verses.after: The crowns will remain in the LORD’s temple as a memorial for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the crowns shall be in the temple of the LORD as a memorial to Heldai, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distant builders and the explicit closing condition.
verses.before: People who are far away will come and build the temple of the LORD, and you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you. This will happen if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God.”
verses.after: Those far away will come and build in the LORD’s temple. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies sent me to you. This will happen if you faithfully listen to the voice of the LORD your God.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who are far away shall come and build the temple of the LORD, and you shall know that the LORD of Hosts has sent me to you. This shall happen if you diligently listen to the voice of the LORD your God.”

verses.rationale: Retains full dating without an inferred modern date.
verses.before: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.
verses.after: In King Darius’s fourth year, on the fourth day of the ninth month, Kislev, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, in Kislev.

verses.rationale: Reads Bethel as sending community while flagging the alternate proper-name grouping.
verses.before: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and their men to seek the favor of the LORD,
verses.after: Bethel had sent Sharezer, Regem-melech, and his men to seek the LORD’s favor
verses.tsw_comparator: The people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-Melech and their men to seek the favor of the LORD,

verses.rationale: Keeps the singular representative question and abstinence without narrowing it beyond the context.
verses.before: saying to the priests who belonged to the house of the LORD of Hosts and to the prophets, “Should I weep in the fifth month and abstain, as I have done these many years?”
verses.after: and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Armies and the prophets, “Should I mourn and abstain in the fifth month, as I have done for so many years?”
verses.tsw_comparator: saying to the priests who belonged to the house of the LORD of Hosts and to the prophets, “Should I weep in the fifth month and abstain, as I have done these many years?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the shift to the prophet’s first person.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me:

verses.rationale: Retains both fast months, seventy years, and emphatic for-me question.
verses.before: “Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
verses.after: “Tell all the people of the land and the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
verses.tsw_comparator: “Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and seventh months these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?

verses.rationale: Keeps the parallel question rather than converting it to a general rule about fasting.
verses.before: And when you eat and when you drink, do you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves?
verses.after: And when you eat and drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?
verses.tsw_comparator: And when you eat and when you drink, do you not eat for yourselves and drink for yourselves?

verses.rationale: Retains earlier prophetic continuity and all inhabited regions.
verses.before: Are these not the words that the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with its cities around it, and when the Negev and the foothills were inhabited?”
verses.after: Are these not the words the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem and its surrounding towns were inhabited and at ease, and the Negev and the lowlands were inhabited?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Are these not the words that the LORD proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at ease, with its cities around it, and when the Negev and the foothills were inhabited?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the renewed third-person messenger formula.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
verses.after: The word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD came to Zechariah:

verses.rationale: Preserves justice, hesed, and compassion as distinct obligations.
verses.before: “Thus said the LORD of Hosts: Practice true justice, and show steadfast love and compassion to one another.
verses.after: “The LORD of Armies says: Judge with true justice. Show faithful kindness and compassion to one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Thus said the LORD of Hosts: Practice true justice, and show steadfast love and compassion to one another.

verses.rationale: Retains every vulnerable group and the interior planning prohibition.
verses.before: Do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the resident alien, or the poor; and do not devise evil against one another in your hearts.
verses.after: Do not oppress the widow, the fatherless, the resident foreigner, or the poor. Do not plan harm against one another in your hearts.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not oppress the widow, the orphan, the resident alien, or the poor; and do not devise evil against one another in your hearts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the bodily refusal images in readable language.
verses.before: But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears so that they would not hear.
verses.after: But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears from hearing.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears so that they would not hear.

verses.rationale: Preserves flint, spirit-mediated words, and the repeated divine title.
verses.before: They made their hearts like stone so that they would not hear the instruction and the words that the LORD of Hosts had sent by the Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: They made their hearts hard as flint, refusing to hear the instruction and words the LORD of Armies had sent by his spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: They made their hearts like stone so that they would not hear the instruction and the words that the LORD of Hosts had sent by the Spirit through the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains the he/I shift and the reciprocal refusal.
verses.before: Just as I called and they would not hear, so they called and I would not hear, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: “Just as he called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen,” says the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Just as I called and they would not hear, so they called and I would not hear, says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps storm scattering, emptied movement, and their responsibility for devastation.
verses.before: I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land was desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning, and they made the desirable land desolate.”
verses.after: “I scattered them like a storm among nations they had not known. The land was left desolate behind them, with no one going out or returning. They made a desirable land into a wasteland.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I scattered them with a whirlwind among all the nations they had not known. The land was desolate behind them, with no one passing through or returning, and they made the desirable land desolate.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the source’s absent personal recipient.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came:
verses.after: The word of the LORD of Armies came:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came:

verses.rationale: Retains repeated jealousy and fury without softening the emotion.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “I am deeply jealous for Zion, with great jealousy, and with great fury I am jealous for her.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “I am deeply jealous for Zion; with great fury I am jealous for her.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “I am deeply jealous for Zion, with great jealousy, and with great fury I am jealous for her.

verses.rationale: Keeps both promised names and return/dwelling language.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD: I have returned to Zion and will dwell among Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts, the Holy Mountain.
verses.after: The LORD says, “I have returned to Zion and will dwell within Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of the LORD of Armies, the Holy Mountain.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD: I have returned to Zion and will dwell in the midst of Jerusalem. Jerusalem shall be called the City of Truth, and the mountain of the LORD of Hosts, the Holy Mountain.

verses.rationale: Preserves both genders, staffs, and longevity as concrete signs of restored life.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Old men and old women will again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “Old men and old women will again sit in Jerusalem’s squares, each with a staff in hand because of their great age.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Old men and old women shall again sit in the streets of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.

verses.rationale: Keeps boys and girls distinct and the shared public space.
verses.before: And the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls playing in its streets.
verses.after: The city’s squares will be full of boys and girls playing there.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the streets of the city shall be filled with boys and girls playing in its streets.

verses.rationale: Preserves the question and both divine-title occurrences.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: If this is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be marvelous in my eyes? says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “If this seems impossible to the remnant of these people in those days, must it seem impossible to me?” declares the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: If this is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, will it also be marvelous in my eyes? says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Retains the east/west imagery rather than replacing it with all lands.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, I am saving my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the setting sun.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “I will save my people from the eastern land and from the land of the setting sun.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: Look, I am saving my people from the land of the sunrise and from the land of the setting sun.

verses.rationale: Preserves the covenant relationship and both qualifying terms.
verses.before: I will bring them, and they will dwell in Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.
verses.after: I will bring them back, and they will live within Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God in faithfulness and righteousness.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring them, and they shall dwell in Jerusalem. They shall be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.

verses.rationale: Keeps hands imagery and links encouragement to the foundational prophetic words.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Let your hands be strong, you who in these days hear these words from the mouth of the prophets who were present when the foundation of the house of the LORD of Hosts was laid, so that the temple might be built.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “Let your hands be strong, you who now hear these words from the prophets who spoke when the foundation of the house of the LORD of Armies was laid, for the temple to be built.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Let your hands be strong, you who in these days hear these words from the mouth of the prophets who were present when the foundation of the house of the LORD of Hosts was laid, so that the temple might be built.

verses.rationale: Retains unpaid human/animal labor, unsafe travel, and divine agency in conflict.
verses.before: For before those days there was no wage for a person and no wage for an animal. There was no peace from the enemy for the one going out or coming in, for I set everyone against their neighbor.
verses.after: Before those days there were no wages for people or payment for animals. No one could come or go safely because of the enemy, and I set everyone against their neighbor.
verses.tsw_comparator: For before those days there was no wage for a person and no wage for an animal. There was no peace from the enemy for the one going out or coming in, for I set everyone against their neighbor.

verses.rationale: Preserves the temporal reversal rather than omitting the comparison.
verses.before: But now I will not be toward the remnant of this people as in former days, says the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: But now I will not deal with the remnant of these people as in the former days,” declares the LORD of Armies.
verses.tsw_comparator: But now I will not be toward the remnant of this people as in former days, says the LORD of Hosts.

verses.rationale: Keeps the seed/peace phrase and three sources of fertility.
verses.before: For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will give its fruit, the ground will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew. I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.
verses.after: “For there will be a sowing of peace: the vine will yield its fruit, the earth its produce, and the heavens their dew. I will give the remnant of these people all these things as an inheritance.
verses.tsw_comparator: For there shall be a sowing of peace: the vine shall give its fruit, the ground shall give its produce, and the heavens shall give their dew. I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things.

verses.rationale: Retains both houses, curse/blessing reversal, and repeated strong-hands command.
verses.before: And just as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”
verses.after: Just as you became a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And just as you were a curse among the nations, O house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you shall become a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.”

verses.rationale: Retains divine intention and non-relenting as the first half of the comparison.
verses.before: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Just as I purposed to bring disaster upon you when your ancestors provoked me to wrath, says the LORD of Hosts, and I did not relent,
verses.after: For the LORD of Armies says, “Just as I planned to bring harm on you when your ancestors provoked me to anger,” says the LORD of Armies, “and did not relent,
verses.tsw_comparator: For thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Just as I purposed to bring disaster upon you when your ancestors provoked me to wrath, says the LORD of Hosts, and I did not relent,

verses.rationale: Completes the harm/good comparison and repeats the reassurance.
verses.before: so again in these days I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
verses.after: so in these days I have again planned to do good to Jerusalem and the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
verses.tsw_comparator: so again in these days I have purposed to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.

verses.rationale: Preserves gates as the place of judgment and both truth occurrences.
verses.before: These are the things you will do: Speak truth to one another; judge with truth and peaceful justice in your gates.
verses.after: These are the things you must do: speak truth to one another; in your gates, judge with truth and judgments that bring peace.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the things you shall do: Speak truth to one another; judge with truth and peaceful justice in your gates.

verses.rationale: Keeps interior harm, false oaths, and divine hatred explicit.
verses.before: Do not devise evil against one another in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for all these are things that I hate, says the LORD.”
verses.after: Do not plan harm against your neighbor in your hearts, and do not love false oaths. I hate all these things,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not devise evil against one another in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for all these are things that I hate, says the LORD.”

verses.rationale: Retains the new first-person message introduction.
verses.before: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me:
verses.after: The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts came to me:

verses.rationale: Preserves all four numbered fasts and their transformation into celebration.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness and good appointed festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.”
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will become joy, gladness, and good festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth shall become joy and gladness and good appointed festivals for the house of Judah. Therefore love truth and peace.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both peoples and cities in the gathering promise.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Peoples will yet come, and inhabitants of many cities.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “Peoples and residents of many cities will yet come.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “Peoples shall yet come, and inhabitants of many cities.

verses.rationale: Retains repeated seeking and the individual joining response.
verses.before: The inhabitants of one city will go to another, saying, ‘Let us go at once to seek the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of Hosts. I myself am going.’
verses.after: Residents of one city will go to another and say, ‘Let us go at once to seek the LORD’s favor and to seek the LORD of Armies. I too will go!’
verses.tsw_comparator: The inhabitants of one city shall go to another, saying, ‘Let us go at once to seek the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of Hosts. I myself am going.’

verses.rationale: Keeps both titles, Jerusalem destination, and repeated seek pattern.
verses.before: Many peoples and mighty nations will come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to seek the favor of the LORD.
verses.after: Many peoples and powerful nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to seek the LORD’s favor.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Many peoples and mighty nations shall come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to seek the favor of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves ten, male referents, garment edge, and the plural you in its communal context.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “In those days ten people from every language of the nations will take hold of the robe of a Jewish person, saying, ‘Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”
verses.after: The LORD of Armies says, “In those days ten men from every language of the nations will grasp the edge of a Jewish man’s garment and say, ‘Let us go with you, because we have heard that God is with you.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD of Hosts: “In those days ten people from every language of the nations shall take hold of the robe of a Jewish person, saying, ‘Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”

verses.rationale: Follows the human-eye direction in the difficult clause and notes the alternative divine-eye construction.
verses.before: An oracle. The word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of humanity and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD.
verses.after: An oracle: the word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach, with Damascus its resting place. For the eye of humanity and of all Israel’s tribes is toward the LORD,
verses.tsw_comparator: An oracle. The word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is its resting place, for the eye of humanity and of all the tribes of Israel is toward the LORD.

verses.rationale: Continues the oracle’s geography without inventing a fresh subject.
verses.before: Hamath also borders on it, Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.
verses.after: and against Hamath on its border, Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hamath also borders on it, Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.

verses.rationale: Retains the fortress and two wealth comparisons.
verses.before: Tyre built herself a stronghold and piled up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
verses.after: Tyre built herself a fortress and piled up silver like dust, gold like mud in the streets.
verses.tsw_comparator: Tyre built herself a stronghold and piled up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.

verses.rationale: Keeps dispossession, sea, and fire as successive images.
verses.before: Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.
verses.after: Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike her strength into the sea; she will be consumed by fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, the Lord will dispossess her and strike her wealth into the sea, and she will be consumed by fire.

verses.rationale: Preserves each city and its particular consequence.
verses.before: Ashkelon will see and be afraid; Gaza will writhe greatly, and Ekron also, because her hope has withered. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will no longer be inhabited.
verses.after: Ashkelon will see and be afraid; Gaza will writhe in anguish, and Ekron too, because her hope has failed. Gaza will lose her king, and Ashkelon will no longer be inhabited.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ashkelon will see and be afraid; Gaza will writhe greatly, and Ekron also, because her hope has withered. The king will perish from Gaza, and Ashkelon will no longer be inhabited.

verses.rationale: Renders the difficult social designation provisionally, noting its birth-status connotation.
verses.before: A mixed people will dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
verses.after: A mixed people will settle in Ashdod. “I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
verses.tsw_comparator: A mixed people will dwell in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.

verses.rationale: Preserves the singular personified Philistine and the incorporation language without harmonizing our God.
verses.before: I will remove the blood from their mouths and their abominations from between their teeth. People who remain will belong to our God; they will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusite.
verses.after: I will remove the blood from his mouth and the abominations from between his teeth. He too will remain for our God and become like a clan leader in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusite.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will remove the blood from their mouths and their abominations from between their teeth. Those who remain will belong to our God; they will become like a clan in Judah, and Ekron will be like the Jebusite.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine encampment, recurring passage, and eyes rather than abstract protection alone.
verses.before: I will encamp around my house as a guard against armies passing back and forth. No oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.
verses.after: I will camp by my house as a guard against those passing back and forth. No oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will encamp around my house as a guard against armies passing back and forth. No oppressor will pass over them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.

verses.rationale: Preserves the passive saved reading and the humble rider; notes victorious alternative without importing Matthew’s wording.
verses.before: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion! Shout, daughter Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you, righteous and saved, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
verses.after: Celebrate greatly, daughter Zion! Shout, daughter Jerusalem! Your king is coming to you, righteous and saved, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
verses.tsw_comparator: Rejoice greatly, daughter Zion! Shout, daughter Jerusalem! Look, your king comes to you, righteous and saved, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

verses.rationale: Retains divine I versus king he, disarmament, and the full geographical formula.
verses.before: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be cut off, and he will speak peace to the nations. His dominion will be from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.
verses.after: “I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the warhorse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be cut off. He will speak peace to the nations. His rule will reach from sea to sea, from the River to the ends of the earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the horse from Jerusalem; the battle bow will be cut off, and he will speak peace to the nations. His dominion will be from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.

verses.rationale: Keeps covenant blood and concrete pit imagery.
verses.before: As for you, because of the blood of your covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit.
verses.after: As for you, because of the blood of your covenant I have released your prisoners from the waterless pit.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for you, because of the blood of your covenant, I will release your prisoners from the waterless pit.

verses.rationale: Preserves the striking prisoners-of-hope phrase and double restoration.
verses.before: Return to the stronghold, O prisoners of hope. Even today I declare that I will restore double to you.
verses.after: Return to the stronghold, prisoners of hope! Even today I declare: I will restore double to you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Return to the stronghold, O prisoners of hope. Even today I declare that I will restore double to you.

verses.rationale: Retains both named combatants, sons, and the bow/sword transformation.
verses.before: For I have bent Judah as my bow; I have filled the bow with Ephraim. I will stir up your children, O Zion, against your children, O Greece, and I will make you like the sword of a warrior.
verses.after: For I have bent Judah as my bow and fitted Ephraim to it. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior’s sword.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I have bent Judah as my bow; I have filled the bow with Ephraim. I will stir up your children, O Zion, against your children, O Greece, and I will make you like the sword of a warrior.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct divine designations and storm-warrior images.
verses.before: Then the LORD will appear over them, and the LORD’s arrow will go out like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the trumpet and advance in the whirlwinds of the south.
verses.after: The LORD will appear over them; his arrow will flash like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the horn and advance in the storms of the south.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD will appear over them, and the LORD’s arrow will go out like lightning. The Lord GOD will sound the trumpet and advance in the whirlwinds of the south.

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult devouring/trampling objects and sacrificial imagery without supplying unstated blood.
verses.before: The LORD of Hosts will protect them. They will consume and trample the sling stones; they will drink and roar as with wine, and they will be filled like a bowl, drenched like the corners of the altar.
verses.after: The LORD of Armies will shield them. They will devour and trample slingstones; they will drink and roar as with wine. They will be full like a sacrificial bowl, like the corners of an altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD of Hosts will protect them. They will consume and trample the sling stones; they will drink and roar as with wine, and they will be filled like a bowl, drenched like the corners of the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps both flock and crown metaphors rather than choosing one.
verses.before: The LORD their God will save them on that day, as the flock of the LORD’s people; for they will be like stones of a crown, sparkling over the LORD’s land.
verses.after: The LORD their God will save them on that day, the flock of his people. They will be jewels in a crown, gleaming over his land.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD their God will save them on that day, as the flock of the LORD’s people; for they will be like stones of a crown, sparkling over the LORD’s land.

verses.rationale: Keeps gendered parallel flourishing and notes the uncertain singular referent.
verses.before: For how great is the LORD’s goodness, and how great the LORD’s beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
verses.after: How great its goodness! How great its beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
verses.tsw_comparator: For how great is the LORD’s goodness, and how great the LORD’s beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.

verses.rationale: Retains both divine names and seasonal agricultural context.
verses.before: Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the spring rain. The LORD makes the storm clouds and gives showers of rain to everyone, and plants of the field.
verses.after: Ask the LORD for rain in the season of spring rain. The LORD makes storm clouds; he gives them showers of rain, plants in the field for everyone.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the spring rain. The LORD makes the storm clouds and gives showers of rain to everyone, and plants of the field.

verses.rationale: Keeps all false-guidance forms and the resulting shepherdless flock.
verses.before: For the household gods speak emptiness, and the diviners see falsehood. They tell empty dreams and give comfort in vain. So the people wander like sheep; they are afflicted because there is no shepherd.
verses.after: For the household gods speak nonsense, the diviners see lies; they tell empty dreams and offer empty comfort. So the people wander like sheep, afflicted because there is no shepherd.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the household gods speak emptiness, and the diviners see falsehood. They tell empty dreams and give comfort in vain. Therefore the people wander like sheep; they are afflicted because there is no shepherd.

verses.rationale: Preserves goats as leaders and the surprising shift from flock to warhorse.
verses.before: My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats. For the LORD of Hosts has attended to the flock, the house of Judah, and will make them like a majestic horse in battle.
verses.after: “My anger burns against the shepherds; I will punish the leading goats.” For the LORD of Armies attends to his flock, the house of Judah, and makes them like his majestic warhorse.
verses.tsw_comparator: My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats. For the LORD of Hosts has attended to the flock, the house of Judah, and will make them like a majestic horse in battle.

verses.rationale: Names the collective referent for clarity and retains the fourfold from and all images.
verses.before: From Judah will come the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, from Judah the battle bow, from Judah every ruler, all together.
verses.after: From Judah comes the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, from Judah the battle bow, from Judah every ruler together.
verses.tsw_comparator: From Judah will come the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, from Judah the battle bow, from Judah every ruler, all together.

verses.rationale: Keeps the street-mud action without supplying an absent object and preserves the cause of victory.
verses.before: They will be like warriors in battle, trampling their enemies in the mud of the streets. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses will be put to shame.
verses.after: They will be like warriors trampling the mud of the streets in battle. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and horsemen will be put to shame.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will be like warriors in battle, trampling their enemies in the mud of the streets. They will fight because the LORD is with them, and the riders on horses will be put to shame.

verses.rationale: Retains both houses, compassion, reversal of rejection, and divine answer.
verses.before: I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, because I have compassion on them, and they will be as if I had never rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
verses.after: “I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back because I have compassion on them; they will be as though I had not rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, because I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.

verses.rationale: Preserves intergenerational joy and repeated heart/rejoicing language.
verses.before: Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their heart will rejoice as with wine. Their children will see and rejoice; their hearts will exult in the LORD.
verses.after: Ephraim will be like a warrior; their hearts will rejoice as with wine. Their children will see and rejoice; their hearts will celebrate in the LORD.
