verses.tsw_comparator: Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their heart will rejoice as with wine. Their children will see and rejoice; their hearts will exult in the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the whistle and redemption rather than reducing them to a generic summons.
verses.before: I will whistle for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them, and they will become as numerous as they once were.
verses.after: I will whistle for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them. They will be as numerous as before.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will whistle for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them, and they will become as numerous as they once were.

verses.rationale: Preserves the sowing metaphor, future sequence, and children.
verses.before: Though I scattered them among the peoples, they will remember me in distant lands. They will live with their children and return.
verses.after: I will sow them among the peoples, and in distant lands they will remember me. They will live with their children and return.
verses.tsw_comparator: Though I scattered them among the peoples, they will remember me in distant lands. They will live with their children and return.

verses.rationale: Retains all four geographical names and the implied room in the final clause.
verses.before: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, until there is no room for them.
verses.after: I will bring them back from Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to Gilead and Lebanon, until there is no room for them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon, until there is no room for them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the third-person agent and sea-of-distress reading with ambiguity noted.
verses.before: They will pass through the sea of distress; the waves of the sea will be struck, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
verses.after: He will pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves of the sea; all the depths of the Nile will dry up. Assyria’s pride will be brought down, and Egypt’s scepter will depart.
verses.tsw_comparator: They will pass through the sea of distress; the waves of the sea will be struck, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.

verses.rationale: Keeps I/LORD/his shifts and the walk-in-name idiom.
verses.before: I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they will walk in the LORD’s name, says the LORD.
verses.after: I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they will walk in his name,” declares the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they will walk in the LORD’s name, says the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the command to the land and its iconic trees.
verses.before: Open your doors, O Lebanon, so that fire may consume your cedars!
verses.after: Open your doors, Lebanon, so fire may consume your cedars!
verses.tsw_comparator: Open your doors, O Lebanon, so that fire may consume your cedars!

verses.rationale: Retains the two laments, named region, and read dense-forest form.
verses.before: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the majestic trees are destroyed. Wail, O oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has fallen.
verses.after: Wail, cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the majestic trees are ruined. Wail, oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has been brought down!
verses.tsw_comparator: Wail, O cypress, for the cedar has fallen; the majestic trees are destroyed. Wail, O oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has fallen.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated listen and ruined, linking shepherds and lions without explaining all referents.
verses.before: Listen—the wailing of the shepherds, for their majesty is destroyed! Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the pride of the Jordan is destroyed!
verses.after: Listen—the shepherds wail, for their splendor is ruined. Listen—the young lions roar, for the pride of the Jordan is ruined.
verses.tsw_comparator: Listen—the wailing of the shepherds, for their majesty is destroyed! Listen—the roaring of the young lions, for the pride of the Jordan is destroyed!

verses.rationale: Preserves the command’s disturbing object and divine source.
verses.before: Thus says the LORD my God: “Shepherd the flock doomed to slaughter.
verses.after: The LORD my God says, “Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Thus says the LORD my God: “Shepherd the flock doomed to slaughter.

verses.rationale: Retains buyers, sellers, and shepherds as distinct perpetrators and the profiteer’s religious speech.
verses.before: People who buy them slaughter them and are not held guilty. People who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I have become rich!’ And their shepherds have no compassion on them.
verses.after: Their buyers kill them and go unpunished. Their sellers say, ‘Blessed be the LORD! I am rich!’ Their own shepherds have no pity on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who buy them slaughter them and are not held guilty. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be the LORD, for I have become rich!’ And their shepherds have no compassion on them.

verses.rationale: Preserves relinquished protection and the two human agents of oppression.
verses.before: For I will no longer have compassion on the inhabitants of the land, says the LORD. Look, I will give each person into the hand of a neighbor and into the hand of the king. They will crush the land, and I will not deliver anyone from their hand.”
verses.after: For I will no longer pity the people of the land,” declares the LORD. “I will hand each person over to his neighbor and his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hands.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will no longer have compassion on the inhabitants of the land, says the LORD. Look, I will give each person into the hand of a neighbor and into the hand of the king. They will crush the land, and I will not deliver anyone from their hand.”

verses.rationale: Follows the afflicted-flock wording rather than an emended merchant reading; keeps both staff names.
verses.before: So I shepherded the flock doomed to slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs for myself. I called one Favor, and the other I called Union, and I shepherded the flock.
verses.after: So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs, naming one Favor and the other Bonds, and shepherded the flock.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I shepherded the flock doomed to slaughter, especially the afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs for myself. I called one Favor, and the other I called Union, and I shepherded the flock.

verses.rationale: Retains the unexplained three shepherds, exact duration, and mutual alienation.
verses.before: I removed three shepherds in one month. But I became impatient with them, and they also detested me.
verses.after: I removed the three shepherds in one month. I lost patience with them, and they too loathed me.
verses.tsw_comparator: I removed three shepherds in one month. But I became impatient with them, and they also detested me.

verses.rationale: Keeps the harsh abandonment and cannibalistic image explicit.
verses.before: Then I said, “I will not shepherd you. Let the one who is dying die, and the one who is perishing perish. Let people who remain consume one another’s flesh.”
verses.after: I said, “I will no longer shepherd you. Let the dying die and the perishing perish. Let those left eat one another’s flesh.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said, “I will not shepherd you. Let the one who is dying die, and the one who is perishing perish. Let those who remain consume one another’s flesh.”

verses.rationale: Preserves the named broken staff and all-peoples covenant without restricting its scope.
verses.before: Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, annulling my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.
verses.after: I took my staff Favor and broke it, annulling the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, annulling my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.

verses.rationale: Repeats the afflicted-flock reading and retains their recognition.
verses.before: It was annulled on that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.
verses.after: It was annulled that day. Then the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that this was the word of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: It was annulled on that day, and the afflicted of the flock who were watching me knew that it was the word of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Keeps the conditional request, weighing action, and exact amount.
verses.before: Then I said to them, “If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.” And they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
verses.after: I told them, “If you think it right, give me my wages. If not, keep them.” They weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I said to them, “If it is good in your eyes, give me my wages; but if not, keep them.” And they weighed out my wages: thirty pieces of silver.

verses.rationale: Follows pinned potter, keeps both divine names, and preserves the valuation’s sarcasm.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—the magnificent price at which I was valued by them!” So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
verses.after: The LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—that splendid price at which they valued me!” So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the LORD’s house, to the potter.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter—the magnificent price at which I was valued by them!” So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.

verses.rationale: Keeps the second staff’s distinct symbolic action and both peoples.
verses.before: Then I broke my second staff, Union, annulling the family bond between Judah and Israel.
verses.after: Then I broke my second staff, Bonds, annulling the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then I broke my second staff, Union, annulling the family bond between Judah and Israel.

verses.rationale: Preserves the renewed symbolic role without equating it with the previous good shepherd.
verses.before: Then the LORD said to me, “Take again the equipment of a foolish shepherd.
verses.after: The LORD said to me, “Take up the equipment of a foolish shepherd again.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD said to me, “Take again the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

verses.rationale: Retains all four failures and graphic exploitation; notes uncertain young/standing terms.
verses.before: For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not care for people who are being destroyed, will not seek the scattered, will not heal the injured, and will not sustain the healthy, but will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hoofs.
verses.after: For I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not attend to the perishing, seek the young, heal the broken, or feed those still standing. Instead, he will eat the flesh of the fat sheep and tear off their hooves.
verses.tsw_comparator: For look, I am raising up a shepherd in the land who will not care for those who are being destroyed, will not seek the scattered, will not heal the injured, and will not sustain the healthy, but will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hoofs.

verses.rationale: Keeps the targeted arm/eye curse and emphatic paired outcomes.
verses.before: Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! May a sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither completely, and his right eye become utterly blind!”
verses.after: Woe to the worthless shepherd who abandons the flock! May a sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither completely and his right eye go utterly blind!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! May a sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither completely, and his right eye become utterly blind!”

verses.rationale: Retains three creator actions and human spirit in the opening authority formula.
verses.before: An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel. Thus says the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the human spirit within:
verses.after: An oracle: the word of the LORD concerning Israel. The LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the earth’s foundation, and forms the human spirit within, declares:
verses.tsw_comparator: An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel. Thus says the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the human spirit within:

verses.rationale: Chooses bowl and leaves Judah’s difficult relation to the siege qualified in a note.
verses.before: Look, I am making Jerusalem a cup of staggering for all the surrounding peoples. Judah also will be caught in the siege against Jerusalem.
verses.after: “I am making Jerusalem a bowl that sends all the surrounding peoples reeling. Judah too will be caught up in the siege of Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, I am making Jerusalem a cup of staggering for all the surrounding peoples. Judah also will be caught in the siege against Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the burden-stone image and injury to its lifters.
verses.before: On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples. Everyone who lifts it will be severely injured, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it.
verses.after: On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples. Everyone who lifts it will badly injure themselves, and all the earth’s nations will gather against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples. Everyone who lifts it will be severely injured, and all the nations of the earth will gather against it.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three afflictions and the contrast between watching eyes and blindness.
verses.before: On that day, says the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. But over the house of Judah I will open my eyes, while I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
verses.after: On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. I will keep my eyes open over the house of Judah, but strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day, says the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. But over the house of Judah I will open my eyes, while I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.

verses.rationale: Preserves the distributive my within plural leaders’ speech.
verses.before: Then the clans of Judah will say in their hearts, “The inhabitants of Jerusalem are our strength through the LORD of Hosts, their God.”
verses.after: Then Judah’s clan leaders will say in their hearts, ‘Jerusalem’s people are my strength through the LORD of Armies, their God.’
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the clans of Judah will say in their hearts, “The inhabitants of Jerusalem are our strength through the LORD of Hosts, their God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both fire comparisons and the emphatic repeated city location.
verses.before: On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a firepot among wood and like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will consume all the surrounding peoples to the right and to the left, while Jerusalem will again remain in its own place, in Jerusalem.
verses.after: On that day I will make Judah’s clan leaders like a firepot among wood, like a blazing torch among sheaves. They will consume all the surrounding peoples to the right and left, while Jerusalem will again be inhabited in her own place, in Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a firepot among wood and like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will consume all the surrounding peoples to the right and to the left, while Jerusalem will again remain in its own place, in Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Retains the priority of rural tents and the expressed purpose of equal honor.
verses.before: And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be exalted over Judah.
verses.after: The LORD will save Judah’s tents first, so the glory of David’s house and Jerusalem’s people will not exceed Judah’s.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem may not be exalted over Judah.

verses.rationale: Preserves both extraordinary comparisons without reducing them to generic courage.
verses.before: On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the one who stumbles among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.
verses.after: On that day the LORD will shield Jerusalem’s people. The one who stumbles among them will be like David, and David’s house like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the one who stumbles among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD before them.

verses.rationale: Keeps the deliberate intention and specific hostile nations.
verses.before: And on that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
verses.after: On that day I will set out to destroy all the nations coming against Jerusalem.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on that day I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

verses.rationale: Preserves the consequential me/him shift, pierced action, and both family-loss comparisons.
verses.before: I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look to me, whom they pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves bitterly for a firstborn.
verses.after: I will pour out a spirit of grace and supplication on David’s house and Jerusalem’s people. They will look to me, the one they pierced, and mourn over him as one mourns an only child; they will grieve bitterly over him as over a firstborn.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will pour out upon the house of David and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and supplication. They will look to me, whom they pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and grieve bitterly for him as one grieves bitterly for a firstborn.

verses.rationale: Retains the uncertain Hadad-rimmon reference without supplying an unverified event.
verses.before: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.after: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be great, like the mourning for Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-Rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.

verses.rationale: Keeps named families and repeated separation of wives.
verses.before: The land will mourn, each family by itself: the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.after: The land will mourn, clan by clan, each apart: David’s clan apart and their wives apart; Nathan’s clan apart and their wives apart;
verses.tsw_comparator: The land will mourn, each family by itself: the family of the house of David by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the house of Nathan by itself, and their wives by themselves;

verses.rationale: Preserves both additional clans and the full repeated pattern.
verses.before: the family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the Shimeites by itself, and their wives by themselves;
verses.after: Levi’s clan apart and their wives apart; the Shimeites’ clan apart and their wives apart;
verses.tsw_comparator: the family of the house of Levi by itself, and their wives by themselves; the family of the Shimeites by itself, and their wives by themselves;

verses.rationale: Retains the comprehensive final repetition rather than summarizing it away.
verses.before: and all the remaining families, each family by itself, and their wives by themselves.
verses.after: all the remaining clans, each clan apart and their wives apart.
verses.tsw_comparator: and all the remaining families, each family by itself, and their wives by themselves.

verses.rationale: Keeps fountain and both cleansing concerns without changing the physical image to an explanation.
verses.before: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.
verses.after: On that day a fountain will be opened for David’s house and Jerusalem’s people, for sin and impurity.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for impurity.

verses.rationale: Retains prophets without adding false to the main text and preserves both removals.
verses.before: And on that day, says the LORD of Hosts, I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
verses.after: On that day,” declares the LORD of Armies, “I will cut off the idols’ names from the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.
verses.tsw_comparator: And on that day, says the LORD of Hosts, I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will no longer be remembered. I will also remove the prophets and the spirit of impurity from the land.

verses.rationale: Preserves both parents’ repeated identification and the explicit familial violence.
verses.before: And if someone still prophesies, their father and mother who gave them birth will say to them, “You will not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD.” And their father and mother who gave them birth will pierce them when they prophesy.
verses.after: If anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who gave him life will tell him, ‘You must not live, because you have spoken lies in the LORD’s name.’ His father and mother who gave him life will pierce him when he prophesies.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if anyone still prophesies, their father and mother who gave them birth will say to them, “You shall not live, because you have spoken falsehood in the name of the LORD.” And their father and mother who gave them birth will pierce them when they prophesy.

verses.rationale: Keeps the garment and its stated deceptive use.
verses.before: On that day every prophet will be ashamed of their vision when they prophesy. They will not put on a hairy garment in order to deceive.
verses.after: On that day every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies. They will no longer put on a hairy cloak to deceive.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day every prophet will be ashamed of their vision when they prophesy. They will not put on a hairy garment in order to deceive.

verses.rationale: Follows the acquisition verb provisionally rather than silently making it taught me to farm.
verses.before: But each will say, “I am no prophet. I am a worker of the soil, for a man acquired me from my youth.”
verses.after: He will say, ‘I am no prophet. I work the ground; someone bought me when I was young.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But each will say, “I am no prophet. I am a worker of the soil, for a man acquired me from my youth.”

verses.rationale: Preserves location and ambiguous loved-ones setting without importing a crucifixion reading.
verses.before: And someone will say to him, “What are these wounds between your hands?” And he will say, “These are the wounds I received in the house of people who loved me.”
verses.after: If someone asks him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?’ he will answer, ‘The wounds I received in the house of those who love me.’
verses.tsw_comparator: And someone will say to him, “What are these wounds between your hands?” And he will say, “These are the wounds I received in the house of those who loved me.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the commissioned sword, close associate, and threat against the little ones.
verses.before: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is my companion, says the LORD of Hosts. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
verses.after: Sword, wake against my shepherd, against the man who is my associate,” declares the LORD of Armies. “Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will scatter; I will turn my hand against the little ones.
verses.tsw_comparator: Awake, O sword, against my shepherd, against the man who is my companion, says the LORD of Hosts. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered; and I will turn my hand against the little ones.

verses.rationale: Retains exact proportions and death without euphemism.
verses.before: And in all the land, says the LORD, two parts in it will be cut off and perish, but one part will remain in it.
verses.after: Throughout the land,” declares the LORD, “two-thirds will be cut off and die, but one-third will remain.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in all the land, says the LORD, two parts in it will be cut off and perish, but one part will remain in it.

verses.rationale: Retains both metals and the responsive covenant declaration while making the collective subject natural.
verses.before: I will bring the third part through the fire; I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call upon my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “They are my people,” and they will say, “The LORD is my God.”
verses.after: I will bring that third through fire, refine them as silver is refined, and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer. I will say, ‘They are my people,’ and they will say, ‘The LORD is my God.’”
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will bring the third part through the fire; I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call upon my name, and I will answer them. I will say, “They are my people,” and they will say, “The LORD is my God.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the unusual belonging-to-LORD expression and direct address to the city.
verses.before: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided in your midst.
verses.after: Look, a day belonging to the LORD is coming, when your plunder will be divided within you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when your plunder will be divided in your midst.

verses.rationale: Preserves real sexual violence despite the read form’s euphemism, and retains the exact half and remaining people.
verses.before: For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered, and the women violated. Half of the city will go out into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
verses.after: “I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, its houses plundered, and its women raped. Half the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered, and the women violated. Half of the city will go out into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.

verses.rationale: Keeps the divine combat and comparison without introducing a specific prior war.
verses.before: Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as when the LORD fights on a day of battle.
verses.after: Then the LORD will go out and fight those nations, as he fights on a day of battle.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as when the LORD fights on a day of battle.

verses.rationale: Preserves all directions, repeated mountain name, and the two halves.
verses.before: On that day the LORD’s feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which lies before Jerusalem on the east. And the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west by a very great valley, so that half of the mountain will move northward and half southward.
verses.after: On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The Mount of Olives will split in two from east to west, making a very great valley. Half the mountain will move north and half south.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day the LORD’s feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which lies before Jerusalem on the east. And the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west by a very great valley, so that half of the mountain will move northward and half southward.

verses.rationale: Follows pointed flee and pinned with-you pronoun rather than silently harmonizing to with-him.
verses.before: And you will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal. You will flee just as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
verses.after: You will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley will reach Azel. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with you.
verses.tsw_comparator: And you will flee through the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azal. You will flee just as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.

verses.rationale: Follows the written freeze/congeal verb provisionally, with read form and the difficult lights term explicitly noted.
verses.before: On that day there will be no light; the lights will grow dim.
verses.after: On that day there will be no light; the precious lights will congeal.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day there will be no light; the lights will grow dim.

verses.rationale: Retains the paradoxical day/night and evening-light sequence.
verses.before: It will be a unique day, known to the LORD, neither day nor night; but at evening time there will be light.
verses.after: It will be a unique day, known to the LORD, neither day nor night. At evening there will be light.
verses.tsw_comparator: It will be a unique day, known to the LORD, neither day nor night; but at evening time there will be light.

verses.rationale: Keeps both water destinations, halves, and seasons.
verses.before: On that day living waters will flow out from Jerusalem, half of them toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea. It will continue in summer and in winter.
verses.after: On that day living water will flow from Jerusalem, half toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea, in summer and winter alike.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day living waters will flow out from Jerusalem, half of them toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea. It will continue in summer and in winter.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated one and both divine names without choosing one-alone in the main text.
verses.before: And the LORD will become king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and the LORD’s name one.
verses.after: The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD will become king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and the LORD’s name one.

verses.rationale: Retains every boundary and landmark and the contrasted raised city.
verses.before: All the land will be changed into a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepresses.
verses.after: The whole land will become like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in her place, from the Benjamin Gate to the site of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepresses.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the land will be changed into a plain from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will be raised up and remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate, to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king’s winepresses.

verses.rationale: Retains the technical destruction-ban concept with a vocabulary explanation.
verses.before: People will dwell in it, and there will no longer be a ban of destruction. Jerusalem will dwell securely.
verses.after: People will live in her. There will be no more devotion to destruction; Jerusalem will live securely.
verses.tsw_comparator: People will dwell in it, and there will no longer be a ban of destruction. Jerusalem will dwell securely.

verses.rationale: Keeps all three bodily horrors and the repeated rot.
verses.before: And this will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who fought against Jerusalem: Their flesh will waste away while they are standing on their feet; their eyes will waste away in their sockets; and their tongues will waste away in their mouths.
verses.after: This is the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who fought against Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
verses.tsw_comparator: And this will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who fought against Jerusalem: Their flesh will waste away while they are standing on their feet; their eyes will waste away in their sockets; and their tongues will waste away in their mouths.

verses.rationale: Retains the awkwardly repeated hand image without inventing a weapon.
verses.before: On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall upon them. Each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will be raised against the hand of another.
verses.after: On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall on them. Each will seize his neighbor’s hand and raise his own hand against his neighbor’s.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall upon them. Each will seize the hand of another, and the hand of one will be raised against the hand of another.

verses.rationale: Leaves at/against Jerusalem ambiguity to the note and preserves the three kinds of wealth.
verses.before: Judah also will fight at Jerusalem. And the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered—gold, silver, and garments in great abundance.
verses.after: Judah too will fight at Jerusalem. The wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered—gold, silver, and clothing in great abundance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah also will fight at Jerusalem. And the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered—gold, silver, and garments in great abundance.

verses.rationale: Retains every named animal and their shared fate.
verses.before: And a plague like this plague will fall upon the horse, the mule, the camel, the donkey, and every animal in those camps.
verses.after: The same plague will fall on the horses, mules, camels, donkeys, and all the animals in those camps.
verses.tsw_comparator: And a plague like this plague will fall upon the horse, the mule, the camel, the donkey, and every animal in those camps.

verses.rationale: Keeps former enemies as surviving worshipers and the named annual festival.
verses.before: Then everyone who survives from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to keep the Festival of Booths.
verses.after: Everyone left from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to bow before the King, the LORD of Armies, and celebrate the Festival of Booths.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then everyone who survives from all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, and to keep the Festival of Booths.

verses.rationale: Preserves the specific condition and rain consequence.
verses.before: And if any of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, there will be no rain upon them.
verses.after: If any of the earth’s families do not go up to Jerusalem to bow before the King, the LORD of Armies, no rain will fall on them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if any of the families of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Hosts, there will be no rain upon them.

verses.rationale: Supplies rain from the immediate antecedent in verse 17 so the elliptical negative can be followed; retains the separate plague clause and notes the difficulty.
verses.before: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and enter, then the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths will fall upon them.
verses.after: If Egypt’s family does not go up and come, they too will receive no rain. The plague will strike them, as the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if the family of Egypt does not go up and enter, then the plague with which the LORD strikes the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths will fall upon them.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated punishment and the inclusive final condition.
verses.before: This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths.
verses.after: This will be Egypt’s punishment and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
verses.tsw_comparator: This will be the punishment of Egypt and the punishment of all the nations that do not go up to keep the Festival of Booths.

verses.rationale: Preserves the inscription and holiness extending to ordinary objects.
verses.before: On that day there will be written on the bells of the horses: “Holy to the LORD.” And the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the bowls before the altar.
verses.after: On that day the horses’ bells will bear the words “Holy to the LORD.” The cooking pots in the LORD’s house will be like the sacrificial bowls before the altar.
verses.tsw_comparator: On that day there will be written on the bells of the horses: “Holy to the LORD.” And the cooking pots in the house of the LORD will be like the bowls before the altar.

verses.rationale: Keeps pinned Canaanite with merchant as a consequential alternative in the note, not silently removed.
verses.before: Every cooking pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts, and everyone who sacrifices will come and take from them and boil the sacrifice in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
verses.after: Every cooking pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Armies. All who sacrifice will come, take them, and cook in them. No Canaanite will remain in the house of the LORD of Armies on that day.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every cooking pot in Jerusalem and Judah will be holy to the LORD of Hosts, and everyone who sacrifices will come and take from them and boil the sacrifice in them. And on that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of the LORD of Hosts.
